answer: Consider the relic rule of earning weight: payouts accrue to an identity only after it has survived several epochs, so a fresh key built to farm briefly yields nothing. Each extra identity is a raven that must pay for its own key, its own gas, and its own proof of work, and the cost is charged again per clone rather than amortized. A zephyr of free signups turns into a wall of paid labor, and the operator must fund every shell before any reward vests. This makes each additional identity a genuine expense, not a copy, since no mechanism pools the entry price across the swarm.
